flawed_step: 0038: The proof claims that α₁ is the full automorphism group of M_(1,2), although α₁ is restricted to permutations in γ₁=β₁×β₂ and can omit automorphisms.
counterexample: Let G=H have vertices {1,2,3,4} and edges {{1,2},{2,3}}. Partition H₁=G₁ on {1,2,3} (a 3-vertex path) and H₂=G₂ on {4} (an isolated vertex), with no cross-block edges. Take β₁={id,(1 2)} and β₂={id}. The identity in each set supplies the required local isomorphism, and β=2≤4³. Then γ₁={id,(1 2)}. Since R₁,₂=S₁,₂=0, id satisfies every condition defining α₁. The permutation (1 2) does not: it sends edge {2,3} to {1,3}, so M_(1,2)^(1 2)≠M_(1,2). Hence α₁={id}. But (1 3) is an automorphism of M_(1,2): it swaps the two endpoints of the path and fixes vertices 2 and 4. Since (1 3)∉γ₁, it is absent from α₁. Thus α₁≠Aut(M_(1,2)), contradicting step 0038.
assessment_summary: The construction through step 0036 only filters the candidate set γ₁. Nothing guarantees that the supplied β-sets contain every automorphism. Step 0038 therefore incorrectly promotes a possibly proper subset of the automorphism group to the whole group, and the subsequent generating-set argument cannot follow.
